name: Swahili pronouns and verb prefixes
explanation: In Swahili, verbs are built using a pattern: subject prefix + tense prefix + verb root. The subject prefix comes from the pronoun. For example: ni + na + soma = ninasoma (I am reading). Learning these prefixes is key to understanding and forming sentences.

cards.explanation: Mimi means "I". The verb prefix is ni-. Example: ninasoma (I am reading).
Wewe means "you" (one person). The verb prefix is u-. Example: unasoma (you are reading).
Yeye means "he" or "she". The verb prefix is a-. Example: anasoma (he/she is reading).
Sisi means "we". The verb prefix is tu-. Example: tunasoma (we are reading).
Ninyi means "you" (more than one person). The verb prefix is m-. Example: mnasoma (you all are reading).
Wao means "they". The verb prefix is wa-. Example: wanasoma (they are reading).

cards.sw: subject prefix + tense prefix + verb root
cards.explanation: Example: ni + na + soma = ninasoma (I am reading). This structure is used for most verbs in present tense.
